Password reset

Members who forget their password sign back in by a link in an email, without asking support.

Related documents

  • docsTech spec: reset links and tokensHow it is built
  • docsDesign: the reset screensScreens and wording
  • 900 a month → under 200Fewer support requests about forgotten passwords
  • 1 day → under 10 minMembers back in sooner

Scope

Actors

  • MemberForgets their password and signs back in by themselves
  • Support agentPoints members to the reset and checks its history
  • OperatorWatches the number of resets and signs of abuse

The system

Starting a reset from the sign-in screenAn email with a link that works onceA screen to choose a new passwordA notice that the password changedSupport's history of resets

Out of scope

  • Checking who someone is by SMS or phone
  • Changing the registered email
  • Signing in without a password, such as passkeys

Functional requirements

FR = Functional Requirement, AC = Acceptance Criteria

Must

FR-1Member

Start a reset from the sign-in screen

  1. AC1A member who cannot sign in, they enter their registered email and send itan email with a reset link arrives within 5 minutes

FR-2Member

Send a link that works once to the registered email

  1. AC1A member who cannot sign in, they enter their registered email and send itan email with a reset link arrives within 5 minutes
  2. AC2someone enters an email that is not registeredthe screen shows the same words as for a registered one, and no email is sent

FR-3Member

Choose a new password from the link and stay signed in

Sessions on other devices end

  1. AC1A member signed in on another device too, they choose a new password from the linkthey are signed in, and the other session ends

Should

FR-4Member

Tell the member by email that the password changed

  1. AC1a member changes their passworda notice arrives at their email

FR-5Support agent

See a member's history of resets

No acceptance criteria

Could

FR-6Operator

See the number of resets by month

No acceptance criteria

Non-functional requirements

NFR = Non-Functional Requirement

Must

NFR-1Performance

The email arrives soon after it is sent

under 5 min

  1. AC1A member who cannot sign in, they enter their registered email and send itan email with a reset link arrives within 5 minutes

NFR-2Security

A link ends soon and works once

30 min, once

  1. AC1A member with a reset link, they open it a second time, or 31 minutes after it was sentthe screen says the link has ended and offers to send another

NFR-3Security

The screens never tell whether an email is registered

  1. AC1someone enters an email that is not registeredthe screen shows the same words as for a registered one, and no email is sent

Should

NFR-4Availability

99.9% a month

No acceptance criteria

NFR-5Usability

360px wide

  1. AC1a member goes through every step on a phone 360px widenothing scrolls sideways

Background

Today a member who forgets their password can only ask support. Support checks who they are and sends a temporary password, which takes a day on average.

Last month 30% of support requests, about 900, were this, and some members stopped using the service meanwhile.

Constraints

  • Emails go out through the mail provider in use today
  • Members' data stays in today's database
  • It ships in the release at the end of June

Glossary

Reset link
The link in the email to a screen that sets a new password, good for one use
Notice
The email that tells a member their password changed, with the time and the device

Open questions

  1. May members with two-step sign-in reset by the email link alone?Answers: Security team
  2. How long is the history of resets (FR-5) kept?Answers: Support lead

Release plan

It goes to 5% of members first, then to everyone after a week without a rise in support requests.
